clue.text: Report on car trip, getting hit on off side

parts.note: a journalist covers a story when reporting on it
a drive is a journey by car

explanation.surface: A news item about a motoring outing, somehow involving a blow on the off side.
explanation.walkthrough: A cover drive is a cricket stroke played through the off side, the side of the field the batsman faces.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this stroke is a classic attacking shot struck through the off side of the field.

clue.text: Judge hasn't finished the Spanish port

indicators.note: the port's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Cadiz is a port in south-west Spain

explanation.surface: A magistrate abandons a trip before reaching a harbour in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' removes the Z from CADIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadi is a magistrate in a Muslim community who rules according to Islamic law.

clue.text: Sport making 11 pointlessly cheerful

indicators.note: the compass point W is dropped from the state's abbreviation

parts.note: the answer to 11 Down is a US state abbreviated W.Va.
riant is a literary word for smiling or cheerful

explanation.surface: A game that turns a cross-reference into something merely jolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to 11 Down; its traditional abbreviation W.Va. loses W (west, a compass point) to leave VA. 'Sport' is the biologist's word for a mutant, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sport is an organism showing a sudden deviation from type, a mutant form.

clue.text: A role in army's set out for them

definitions.text: A role in army's set out for them

indicators.note: the letters of these words are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A job in the army has been arranged for certain soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges the letters of A ROLE IN ARMY'S, and the whole clue describes the answer: a part in the forces fit for these men.
explanation.definitionFit: These commandos are seaborne soldiers serving with Britain's navy, so a role in an army suits them.

clue.text: Tramp dividing large quantity in big bottle

indicators.note: the vagrant's word sits within the word for a large amount, splitting it

parts.note: a ream is a large amount, literally 500 sheets of paper
a hobo is a vagrant or tramp

explanation.surface: A vagrant splitting a hoard of drink found in a huge bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' signals one word splitting the other; 'Tramp' looks like a verb but is the vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is an outsize wine bottle holding about six standard bottles.

clue.text: It comes between Rex and his adversaries in some cases

definitions.text: It comes between Rex and his adversaries in some cases

parts.words: It comes between Rex and his adversaries in some cases
parts.note: Rex is the Crown in English criminal prosecutions, and the case title names it against the defendant with a Latin word in the middle

explanation.surface: Something seems to come between a man called Rex and his foes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like someone's name, but it is the King as prosecutor, and 'cases' are law cases, as in Rex v Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word meaning against, abbreviated v, separates the parties in the title of a legal action.

clue.text: King of Israel ishmael served under

explanation.surface: A biblical king appears to have had a famous sailor under him.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the wicked biblical ruler married to Jezebel; the other is the captain of the Pequod in Moby-Dick, where Ishmael is a crewman.

clue.text: Complex including a sort of bible college

indicators.note: the word for complex surrounds the other letters

parts.note: hard means difficult or complex
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A complicated place of learning houses an edition of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' signals the container; RV, the Revised Version, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard is the oldest university in the United States, founded as a college in Massachusetts.

clue.text: Money committee provided for dealing with bloomers

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A funding committee has been set up to handle embarrassing mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' are not blunders but loaves: a bloomer is a large British loaf with slashes on top. 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This wooden board is where loaves are sliced, so it is the item used in handling them.

clue.text: Racehorse peaks here

parts.note: the Derby is the famous flat race run at Epsom
a shire is a heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: A horse famed for speed is apparently found among the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racehorse' splits into race and horse. Derbyshire is the English county containing the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peak District, a national park of hills and moors, lies mostly in this English county.

clue.text: Release without charges

explanation.surface: Letting someone go without pressing a case against them.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone, and also costing nothing, as in a gratis service.

clue.text: State recommended course for young man and girl

parts.note: the old advice 'Go west, young man' names the direction to follow
Virginia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Advice on what a lad and his girlfriend should study.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'Go west, young man' was popular advice to Americans heading for the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty US states, with Charleston as its capital.

clue.text: No turning back, we hear, with this famous convert

indicators.note: the clue words signal a word that sounds like the one defined

parts.note: a pawl is a catch on a ratchet that stops a wheel turning backwards

explanation.surface: A determined pilgrim refuses to turn back and follow a famous convert.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul of Tarsus was converted on the road to Damascus and took the name Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle was the most celebrated convert to Christianity, after his vision on the Damascus road.

clue.text: Rue arranging duel with bravo

indicators.note: organising the letters of these two words into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone regrets setting up a fight with a hired assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' looks like the verb regret, but it is French for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A rue in a French town is a street, and a boulevard is a broad avenue.

clue.text: Saw nothing wrong in capital

indicators.note: the letters are put in an incorrect, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A witness noticed nothing amiss in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SAW NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington DC is the seat of the US federal government.

clue.text: In addition to column, female's written on stars of the past

indicators.note: the woman's word is placed after the stars, as writing follows in an across entry

parts.note: astra is the Latin, the old language, for stars
gal is a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A woman's name has been inscribed on a pillar beside ancient constellations.
explanation.walkthrough: An astragal is a small convex moulding added around a column, usually below the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This moulding is a narrow rounded band fitted to a pillar as an extra architectural detail.

clue.text: Cut outside broadcast to make room for various programmes

indicators.note: the letters are scattered like seed sown broadly
the word loses its last letter, as if shortened

explanation.surface: A TV boss axes an outdoor transmission to free space for other shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims OUTSIDE to OUTSID, and 'broadcast' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the room where radio and TV shows are recorded or transmitted.

clue.text: School's potential loss

explanation.surface: An institution worrying about what it might lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Downside is a Catholic boarding school in Somerset run by Benedictine monks; the word also means a disadvantage or risk.

clue.text: Why bride reveals this cross borne by partners

indicators.note: the words display the answer running through them, letting it show

explanation.surface: A bride wonders why her husband is so angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' signals the answer lying inside WHY BRIDE. 'cross' is a noun: the offspring two different parents produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different breeds or species, a crossbreed bred from a pair.

clue.text: Smaller version of tramp steamer?

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp
a steamer is a boat

explanation.surface: Asking about a scaled-down tramp steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: A bumboat is a small boat that ferries provisions to ships at anchor, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This small craft sells goods and supplies to larger ships lying offshore.

clue.text: Act despotically as ruler on occasion, with abominable mien

parts.note: a do is a party or social occasion

indicators.note: something abominable is horribly wrong, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler sometimes behaves tyrannically, wearing a dreadful expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the ruler after the occasion (in an across entry, on means after), and 'abominable' scrambles the face's look into a possessive word placed between them; 'as' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To lord it over others is to behave in an overbearing, tyrannical way.

clue.text: Raised hat first for top people only

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the word turns it upwards so it reads backwards

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat
1st, with the one as I

explanation.surface: Doffing one's hat first to the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses TILE to ELIT; 1ST is written IST.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist attitude favours a privileged few above everyone else.

clue.text: Way in which fare includes strong drink

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
to fare is to go, travel or get on

explanation.surface: The road along which a meal comes with liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' and 'includes' are linking words here. Stingo is an old name for strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is a dialect term for a potent beer, a strong ale.

clue.text: Political address making issue clear? Just the reverse

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a number

indicators.note: the phrase says to turn the word for clear backwards

parts.note: net means clear, as in net profit

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a political speech clarifies an issue, or does the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' turns NET into TEN. Number Ten, Downing Street, is the British prime minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: 10 Downing Street is the official London home of the British prime minister.

clue.text: Sound opening in pedestrian style

indicators.note: the clue says what follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A good start to a plodding manner of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it signals a word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A gait is a manner of walking, the way a person moves on foot.

clue.text: A lot can be said for this type of entertainment

indicators.note: the word for destiny when spoken resembles the answer

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Much might be said in favour of this kind of amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like a large quantity, but it is one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair or bazaar, often to raise money.

clue.text: Required to give permission

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Being obliged to grant consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Required' is in the past tense: the job took (needed) an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: If something took an hour, it needed or demanded that time.

clue.text: Asian data put in a single column

parts.note: an Indian is a person from India, in Asia
a file is a body of data

explanation.surface: Information from Asia set out in one column of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' is a line of people, not a column of figures; 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in this formation means moving one behind another in a line.

clue.text: Dreadfully unstable? Not half!

indicators.note: only one half of the word, its first four letters, is used

explanation.surface: Someone is asked if they are very unbalanced and replies emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps UNST, the first half of UNSTABLE, and 'Dreadfully' rearranges it; the whole clue also describes the answer, slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for mad, and anyone mad is very unstable mentally.

clue.text: Ship's quarters here for English man on board

parts.note: a castle is a chess piece, also called a rook

explanation.surface: An Englishman on a vessel needs a place to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' looks like a sailor but means a chessman; 'here' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fo'c'sle is the forward part of a vessel where the crew traditionally lived.
